title: Redefining Teacher Leadership in the Age of ChatGPT: Instructional Practices, Ethical Challenges, and Professional Agency in Moroccan High Schools
venue: International Journal of Language and Literary Studies
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative AI, specifically ChatGPT, is being used by high school teachers in Morocco and how that use is reshaping teacher leadership and professional agency. The study is framed by instructional leadership theory and asks how teachers use ChatGPT in lesson planning, activity design, and feedback, what motivates those uses, and how AI affects their classroom leadership roles.

The researchers used a mixed-methods design. Quantitative data came from an online survey of 87 high school teachers in the Casablanca-Settat region, and qualitative data came from semi-structured interviews with 12 teachers plus analysis of ChatGPT-assisted lesson plans. Teachers reported using ChatGPT most often for lesson planning and activity generation, and less often for drafting feedback. The paper argues that teachers are not simply adopting AI passively; they are selectively integrating it where it saves time and supports creativity while retaining human control over evaluative and ethically sensitive tasks.

The findings show three main themes: pedagogical efficiency and creativity, ethical and pedagogical concerns, and leadership/professional agency. Teachers saw ChatGPT as helpful for reducing workload and generating ideas, but they also worried about plagiarism, student overreliance, and occasional inaccuracies in AI outputs. Overall, the study concludes that ChatGPT is reshaping teachers into instructional leaders and ethical gatekeepers who filter AI-generated content through professional judgment. It calls for AI literacy professional development and clearer policy guidance for responsible AI use in Moroccan high schools.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot/large language model system used for conversational text generation and assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by Moroccan high school teachers for lesson planning, classroom activity generation, and drafting feedback on student work; lesson plans developed with ChatGPT were also analyzed.

findings.finding_summary: Among 87 Moroccan high school teachers, 64.4% reported using ChatGPT for lesson planning, 51.7% for activity generation, and 41.4% for drafting feedback. The mixed-methods results indicated teachers viewed ChatGPT as saving time and supporting pedagogical creativity, but they used it more cautiously for evaluative tasks like feedback.
findings.measure: Self-reported ChatGPT use for lesson planning, activity generation, and feedback drafting; interview/document themes on efficiency and creativity

findings.finding_summary: Qualitative findings from 12 interviews and lesson-plan analysis showed ChatGPT supported creativity and differentiated activity design, but teachers also raised concerns about plagiarism, student overreliance, and occasional inaccuracies. Teachers positioned themselves as ethical gatekeepers who filtered outputs before use, indicating selective rather than wholesale adoption.
findings.measure: Interview themes and document analysis of ChatGPT-assisted lesson plans
findings.sample_size: n=12 interviews; lesson plans analyzed from interviewees

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods observational study with survey, interviews, and document analysis rather than an experiment. The evidence is informative but not causal, so it fits the yellow tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports substantial usage and perceived workflow benefits, but it does not provide effect sizes or outcome gains on student learning. Impact is therefore suggestive but unclear at the evidence level.
